title: The platform approach to becoming Frontier
body: The platform approach to becoming Frontier Oct 27, 2026 | Judson Althoff - CEO, Microsoft Commercial Business Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry. Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver. Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites. Empowering human ambition with Copilot Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work . Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition. Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000 . Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually , while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers. KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work . Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily . At Krafton , Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated . By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions. To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses. To transform frontline work, Williams , a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting , while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous . Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier. Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption , and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows. Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents daily with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. title: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia
body: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration is working with NVIDIA to deploy open source AI tools to accelerate the science that makes new treatments possible. October 27, 2026 by Anthony Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. Speeding Research From Weeks to Hours Essential assets in Alzheimer’s research are datasets that have never been publicly accessible to AI tools or human researchers. This includes unpublished findings, negative results and governed proprietary data from member institutions. “A lot of life sciences data doesn’t make its way into the frontier models,” said Dr. Ade Ojewole, chief technology officer of C-BRAIN. “The consequence of that is we’re leaving a lot of intelligence on the table.” C-BRAIN refers to this as “dark data,” which slows down Alzheimer’s research. Some dark data is directly deposited into secure computer systems for AI tools to access. To use this data without compromising patient privacy or institutional governance, C-BRAIN uses a hybrid centralized and federated approach — where AI models learn from data at each institution without that data ever having to leave its walls. This kind of infrastructure is technically demanding to build and scale, which is part of what NVIDIA brings to the collaboration. C-BRAIN currently runs 64 NVIDIA data center GPUs on premises alongside cloud-based nodes on Microsoft Azure, with additional NVIDIA GPU capacity, including NVIDIA Blackwell systems , on the horizon as the consortium’s ambitions scale. To explore how AI and accelerated computing can advance Alzheimer’s research while navigating its technical demands, C-BRAIN is working with NVIDIA to incorporate technologies including the NVIDIA BioNeMo open developer platform and the MONAI framework for C-BRAIN’s research pipelines. “The C-BRAIN collaboration with NVIDIA aims to unlock those models in a way that they can deliver something quite impactful and important,” said Bateman. “A great deal of optimization is going to be needed as we push the boundaries of what today’s spatial omics machine learning architectures can model,” Ojewole said. “NVIDIA software is definitely going to come into play there.” Researchers at C-BRAIN have already built two tools: OpenScientist — built with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in an effort led by research scientist Justin Reese — and InsightEngine , built with 387 Labs. OpenScientist is an open source agentic AI co-scientist that takes a scientist’s research question and dataset, then semi-autonomously generates hypotheses, runs analyses and produces verifiable, auditable insights. InsightEngine is an open source research platform that uses agentic AI to test hypotheses against the scientific literature, analyzing user-supplied datasets, exploring a biomedical knowledge graph and checking every claim against evidence to catch hallucinations before researchers commit to costly experiments. In published case studies, OpenScientist completed analyses in minutes that domain scientists estimated would take weeks to months, at a cost of under $10 per run. At C-BRAIN’s current reach of over 200 research groups, this capability could release substantial research capacity, potentially exceeding one million hours annually at scale. From Correlation to Cause Looking ahead, C-BRAIN aims to build a multimodal biological foundation model trained on the full breadth of its data — neuroimaging, multi-omics, fluid biomarkers and longitudinal clinical measures. By year three, it aims to discover new causal mechanisms of brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, moving to testable scientific principles using the full scope of available research and data. Bateman said, “ AI that can think and reason has the potential to accelerate discoveries that will lead to powerful and implementable preventions and treatments for the entire population.” Categories: AI Tags: Agentic AI AI for Good Healthcare and Life Sciences Open Source Related News AI How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia Oct 27, 2026 AI NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models Oct 21, 2026 AI NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations Oct 21, 2026 AI Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction Oct 21, 2026

title: Davenport Man Sentenced to 340 Months in Federal Prison for Drug and Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Davenport Man Sentenced to 340 Months in Federal Prison for Drug and Firearm Charges Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Davenport man was sentenced on October 27, 2026, to more than 28 years in federal prison for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine, carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking offense, and possessing a firearm as a felon. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, in January 2025, Baylee Andrew Snyder, 29, was found in possession of approximately one pound of methamphetamine and a loaded revolver in his vehicle and a loaded pistol on his person. Snyder admitted that he purchased pound quantities of methamphetamine for distribution in Chicago and worked with others to distribute methamphetamine within the Southern District of Iowa. A few months later, in May 2025, Snyder was arrested again traveling from Chicago to Iowa with multiple pounds of methamphetamine, two loaded firearms, and almost $2,000. Snyder admitted he continued to work with others to distribute pound quantities of methamphetamine in the Southern District of Iowa while carrying multiple firearms for protection. After completing his term of imprisonment, Snyder will be required to serve a five-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Bettendorf Police Department investigated the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. Contact MacKenzie Tubbs Public Information Officer 515-473-9300 USAIAS.PAO@usdoj.gov Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Project Safe Neighborhoods Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Iowa, Southern

title: Florida Inmate Sentenced to Almost Six Additional Years in Prison for Mailing Threatening Communications to a Federal Courthouse
body: Press Release Florida Inmate Sentenced to Almost Six Additional Years in Prison for Mailing Threatening Communications to a Federal Courthouse Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – Alvin Martin Few (age 62) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Wendy W. Berger to five years and eleven months in federal prison for mailing threatening communications. He pleaded guilty on July 14, 2026.  U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, while Few was serving a life sentence plus 15 years for state convictions in Florida, he mailed a letter to the Wilkie D. Ferguson, Jr. U.S. Courthouse in Miami containing threatening statements including “all judges die.” Few put a white powder inside the envelope and wrote that the powder was “very fatal.” A clerk was exposed to the powder when he opened the letter. Lab testing later confirmed the white powder was benign and not a chemical or biological agent. Few’s new federal sentence will run consecutively to his prior life sentence. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Marshals Service. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Richard L. Lasseter. Updated October 27, 2026 Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Personal Assistant Sentenced to 48 Months in Prison for Massive Fraud Scheme Targeting Her Elderly Employers
body: Press Release Personal Assistant Sentenced to 48 Months in Prison for Massive Fraud Scheme Targeting Her Elderly Employers Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Defendant Exploited Her Position of Trust to Steal Nearly $10 Million Which She Spent on Luxury Goods from Louis Vuitton, Gucci, and Cartier Earlier today, at the federal courthouse in Brooklyn, Catalina Corona was sentenced by United States District Judge Nicholas G. Garaufis to 48 months’ imprisonment for wire fraud in connection with a long running scheme to defraud her elderly employers.  As part of her sentence, Corona was also ordered to pay $9.6 million in forfeiture. Corona pleaded guilty to the charge in April 2026. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the sentence. “Today’s sentence holds the defendant accountable for a calculated scheme to steal nearly $10 million from her elderly employers who had entrusted her with their financial affairs for many years,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “With complete control over the victims’ accounts, the defendant was able to siphon large amounts of money at will, and on a breathtaking scale.  Our Office will vigorously prosecute those who exploit vulnerable elderly victims for personal gain.” "Catalina Corona will face justice for her calculated and callus fraud scheme. She swindled nearly $10 million from the elderly couple she was entrusted to assist. Let this be a warning to others that think they may fly under the radar with similar schemes, the FBI will follow the money, and criminals will be found,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. According to court filings and statements in court, Corona began her professional relationship with Victim-1 in the early 2000s when she served as a secretary for Victim-1’s company.  After Victim-1 passed away in May 2022, Corona continued to work as a personal assistant for Victim-1’s wife, Victim-2 (collectively, the “Victims”).  While working as a personal assistant to the Victims, Corona repeatedly deposited hundreds of checks written out to cash—made payable to herself—from the Victims’ bank accounts without their knowledge or consent. In total, Corona stole nearly $10 million, which she used to pay her credit card bills and to purchase luxury items.  Specifically, the investigation revealed that Corona had used approximately $1,117,000 of stolen funds to purchase merchandise at Louis Vuitton, approximately $125,500 to purchase merchandise from Cartier, nearly $300,000 in stolen funds to purchase merchandise at Gucci, and approximately $305,000 in stolen funds to purchase merchandise from Apple. Corona concealed the whereabouts of the high-end luxury items purchased with the stolen funds by renting out two storage units.  Law enforcement obtained search warrants for the defendant’s residence and the two storage units, and estimated that there were over 300 luxury items stashed in the units. The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s General Crimes Section.  Assistant United States  Attorney Rebecca M. Urquiola is in charge of the prosecution. The Defendant : CATALINA CORONA Age: 62 Corona, Queens E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 25-CR-78 (NGG) Contact John Marzulli Denise Taylor United States Attorney’s Office (718) 254-6323 Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Elder Justice Component USAO - New York, Eastern

body: Press Release Panama City Felon Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Gun Possession Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Brian Earl Glass, 37, of Panama City, Florida, has pleaded guilty in federal court on a charge of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the guilty plea. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “The safety of our communities is not negotiable, and we will not yield our streets to dangerous criminals who brazenly violate our laws. President Donald J. Trump and Attorney General Todd Blanche have made clear that we will commit the full might of the Department of Justice toward ensuring that no neighborhood is left behind in our pursuit of crime-free communities for our citizens.” According to court records, during the April 2026 search of a Panama City residence where the defendant was located, the defendant attempted to leave the residence in his vehicle but was detained. Prior to the defendant attempting to leave, investigators had observed a firearm inside the vehicle. The firearm and ammunition were seized. During questioning, the defendant admitted the firearm belonged to him. Records also show that the defendant had multiple prior felony convictions dating back to 2012, and he was therefore legally prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Sentencing is scheduled for January 14, 2027, at 11:00am before United States District Court Judge Mark E. Walker in Tallahassee, Florida. Gainer faces enhanced penalties of up to 15 years’ imprisonment. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin. title: UK Citizen and Chairman of Zetland Fiduciary Group Arrested on a Money Laundering Indictment
body: Press Release UK Citizen and Chairman of Zetland Fiduciary Group Arrested on a Money Laundering Indictment Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — James Sutherland, 77, a citizen of the United Kingdom, made his initial appearance on an indictment on Monday, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. On June 25, 2026, a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of California returned an indictment charging Sutherland with four counts of money laundering. Sutherland is the Chairman of the Zetland Fiduciary Group, a financial services business, with locations in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, and Dubai. According to the indictment, on multiple occasions, Sutherland laundered funds which had been represented to be, and which he believed to be, proceeds generated through computer hacking. “This prosecution highlights our Office’s dedication to working with law enforcement partners around the world to hold money launderers accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Grant. “It is the latest example of our Office’s longstanding efforts to disrupt and dismantle networks that support and promote transnational organized crime.” “Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is uniquely positioned to investigate and disrupt global money laundering and sanctions evasion operations. HSI in Northern California will pursue enablers of criminal and terrorist networks around the world,” said Jeffrey M. Brannigan, Special Agent-in-Charge for Northern California Homeland Security Investigations. “IRS Criminal Investigation special agents are specially equipped to follow the complex financial trail left by criminals, and we are dedicated to holding those accountable for crimes committed,” said Kareem Carter, Executive Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation (CI), Washington, D.C. Field Office. “This indictment sends a clear message that IRS-CI and our law enforcement partners, will remain attentive and we will vigorously pursue those who attempt to enrich themselves through illegal means.” This case was the product of an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations and the IRS Criminal Investigation with support from the Treasury Executive Office for Asset Forfeiture (TEOAF). Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Abendroth is prosecuting the case. If convicted, Sutherland faces a maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison and a $500,000 fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This case is part of the Sacramento Strike Force within the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. The Sacramento Sacrament Strike Force is composed of agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. Marshals Service, DEA, and IRS Criminal Investigation with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California. Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Financial Fraud Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Ukrainian National Sentenced to 70 Months in Prison for Multi-Million Dollar Ransomware Conspiracies
body: Press Release Ukrainian National Sentenced to 70 Months in Prison for Multi-Million Dollar Ransomware Conspiracies Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York $11 Million Reward Remains for Co-Conspirator Still at Large BROOKLYN, NY – Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Artem Stryzhak, a Ukrainian national, was sentenced by United States District Judge Pamela K. Chen to 70 months in prison for using ransomware to extort millions of dollars from victims.  The defendant pled guilty in December 2025 to conspiracy to commit fraud, extortion, and related activity in connection with computers. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York; Gregory W. Kehoe, United States Attorney for the Middle District of Florida; A. Tysen Duva, Assistant Attorney General of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), New York Field Office; Ryan Presley, Special Agent in Charge, FBI, Springfield, Illinois Field Office; and Rodney Crawford, Special Agent in Charge, FBI, Tampa  Florida Division announced the sentence. “Ransomware attacks like those committed by the defendant wreak enormous havoc—harming victim companies that pay millions in remediation and ransoms, preventing hospitals and other critical facilities from accessing data, and putting sensitive information in the hands of bad actors,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Today’s sentence reflects that cybercriminals cannot hide from law enforcement and will face significant punishment for their criminal conduct. We remain determined to capture Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, a serial ransomware developer and Stryzhak’s co-conspirator.” Mr. Nocella expressed his appreciation to the FBI’s New York Field Office for their significant contributions to the investigation.  Mr. Nocella also thanked the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs and Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), as well as Spanish law enforcement authorities, for their assistance in the capture of Stryzhak. “Disrupting a ransomware group that attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide and sentencing a defendant who had targeted healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic is of significant importance to this office,” said U.S. Attorney Kehoe for the Middle District of Florida.  “We are proud of our law enforcement partners for their skilled investigative work in bringing this criminal to justice.” “Artem Stryzhak chose to deploy ransomware that extorted money from victims, leaving businesses and individuals facing devasting losses.  His actions serve as a strong reminder of the real-world damage cybercriminals can cause and underscore the FBI’s commitment to stopping these schemes and protecting the public,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. “Cybercriminals who deploy ransomware inflict real and lasting damage on the communities we serve.  The work leading to today’s sentence reflects the dedication of our agents and partners who spent years untangling a complex, transnational scheme,” stated FBI Springfield Special Agent in Charge Presley. “The FBI Springfield Field Office will continue to pursue actors who target U.S. networks and ensure they are held accountable.  Our pursuit of Volodymyr Tymoshchuk remains ongoing, and we urge anyone with information to come forward.” “Today’s action underscores the FBI’s steadfast commitment to pursuing cyber criminals wherever they operate. This case highlights the effectiveness with which multiple FBI field offices can coordinate to investigate sophisticated intrusions and impose real consequences for malicious activity,” stated FBI Tampa Division Special Agent in Charge Crawford.  “The Tampa FBI Cyber Task Force remains dedicated to working with our domestic and international partners to identify cyber threat actors, disrupt their operations, and ensure justice for the individuals and organizations harmed by these crimes. Because of this collaboration, Stryzhak will be held responsible for his activities as an affiliate of Hive Ransomware.” According to court documents, Stryzhak conspired with others to perpetrate ransomware attacks on behalf of multiple ransomware groups against victim computer networks in the United States and other countries, causing significant damage to victim computer systems.  If a victim paid the ransom demand, the perpetrators provided the decryption key, enabling the victim to decrypt files locked by the ransomware. Beginning in about June 2021, Stryzhak joined the ongoing Nefilim conspiracy as a Nefilim ransomware affiliate. Stryzhak was given access to the Nefilim ransomware and agreed with one of the Nefilim ransomware group administrators, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk , to pay the Nefilim administrators 20% of the ransom proceeds extorted from victims in exchange for Stryzhak’s access to the Nefilim ransomware. The ransomware attacks that Stryzhak conducted with Nefilim ransomware included a June 2021 attack in which Stryzhak stole data from a company in the oil and gas transportation industry.  About a week later, Stryzhak created email addresses that were incorporated in a ransom note sent to the victim company.  Through at least October 2021, Stryzhak deployed Nefilim ransomware. Further, Stryzhak separately joined the Hive ransomware group as one of its earliest affiliates.  From June 2021 to January 2023, Hive conspirators attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide, including government entities, hospitals, and businesses.  Hive ransomware attacks caused major disruptions in victim daily operations around the world and affected responses to the COVID-19 pandemic.  In one case, a hospital attacked by the Hive ransomware group had to forgo digital technology to treat existing patients and was unable to accept new patients immediately following the attack. In his role as a Hive affiliate, Stryzhak and his co-conspirators deployed Hive ransomware against seven victims including law firms, a dentist’s office, and a healthcare provider during the COVID-19 pandemic.  Victims were unable to access their encrypted data.  The FBI, as part of a months-long disruption campaign against the Hive ransomware group , provided a decryption key to one of Stryzhak’s victims, thereby allowing that victim to decrypt its encrypted data without having to pay a ransom. Stryzhak was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the United States on April 30, 2025. The U.S. Department of State’s Transnational Organized Crime (TOC) Rewards Program has offered a reward of up to $11 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction or location of Stryzhak’s charged co-conspirator, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk.  Anyone with information about Tymoshchuk should contact the FBI via phone at +1-917-242-1407, by email at TymoTips@fbi.gov , by contacting your local field office, if in the United States, or by contacting the nearest U.S. Embassy, if located overseas.  More information about the TOC reward offer is located on the State Department website . The FBI Springfield Field Office investigated the Nefilim ransomware case and the FBI Tampa Field Office investigated the Hive ransomware case. The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and Cybercrime Section.  Assistant United States Attorneys Alexander F. Mindlin and Ellen H. Sise of the Eastern District of New York and Trial Attorney James S. Yoon of CCIPS are in charge of the Nefilim ransomware prosecution, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Magdalena St. Surin.  Former CCIPS Trial Attorney Brian Mund also worked on the case.  The Hive ransomware case is being prosecuted by CCIPS Trial Attorneys Alison M. Zitron and Christen M. Gallagher, and by Assistant United States Attorney Hannah Watson of the Middle District of Florida; former Assistant United States Attorney Chauncey Bratt of the Middle District of Florida also worked on the case. The Defendant : ARTEM ALEKSANDROVYCH STRYZHAK Age:  36 Barcelona, Spain E.D.N.Y. title: Gainesville Woman Convicted in $8.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Gainesville Woman Convicted in $8.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Ocala, FL — A federal jury in the Middle District of Florida convicted a Florida woman who owned a durable medical equipment (DME) company and managed several other DME companies for her role in a fraud scheme that took advantage of the elderly and disabled and caused the submission of over $8.6 million in fraudulent claims to Medicare. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Sophie Dufort, 57, of Gainesville, Florida, conspired with Paula Pirone, 70, of Ocala, Florida, and others to submit fraudulent claims to Medicare based on fake doctors’ prescriptions for orthotic braces. Dufort and her co-conspirators illegally purchased these prescriptions from purported marketing companies that engaged in high pressure and manipulative telemarketing calls to get Medicare beneficiaries’ information. When confronted with complaints that the voice on purported call recordings did not match the beneficiaries’ voice, one co-conspirator explained that “some of the calls from overseas would be faked” and used to justify a bogus prescription. The marketing companies then paid medical practitioners to sign prescriptions for orthotic braces without contacting or evaluating the patients, or stole doctor’s credentials to create forged prescriptions, and then sold those prescriptions to Dufort’s and her co-conspirators’ DME companies. Dufort and her co-conspirators then shipped braces to the Medicare beneficiaries and billed Medicare for millions of dollars in claims, despite the fact that the beneficiaries did not want or need the braces and no doctor had examined the beneficiary to determine if they needed the braces. And, as one medical expert testified, use of these combinations of braces could be “very dangerous” for the elderly Medicare population. When people complained and wanted to return the braces, “they would just tell [them] to just get rid of them or . . . just pass them down” so Dufort and her co-conspirators would not have to pay Medicare back. The defendant was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, two counts of health care fraud, one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States and to offer and pay illegal kickbacks, and one count of offering and paying illegal kickbacks.  Dufort faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison for conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, 10 years in prison for each health care fraud count and kickback count, and 5 years in prison for conspiracy to defraud the United States and to offer and pay illegal kickbacks.  A sentencing hearing is scheduled in Jan. 2027.  A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Middle District of Florida U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe and Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. The case was investigated by the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Assistant U.S. Attorney William Hamilton for the Middle District of Florida  and Trial Attorney Jody King of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . title: Tallahassee Serial Felon Pleads Guilty to Federal Drug and Firearms Crimes
body: Press Release Tallahassee Serial Felon Pleads Guilty to Federal Drug and Firearms Crimes Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Marcello Hinojosa, 53, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Protecting our communities from the predations of violent, serial offenders like this defendant is one of the highest duties my office has, and I am proud of the excellent work by my prosecutors to hold him accountable. We will continue to aggressively prosecute every federal offense that occurs in this district until our citizens get the safe, crime-free streets that they deserve.” Court documents reflect that in May 2026, law enforcement conducted a traffic stop of a vehicle driven by the defendant in Tallahassee, Florida. During the traffic stop, it was discovered that the defendant did not have a valid driver’s license and that he was wanted for violations of federal supervised release. The defendant had been convicted of federal drug trafficking charges in 2018 and served a term of imprisonment, after which he was placed on supervised release but had subsequently violated the conditions of his supervision. During the search of the defendant’s vehicle, investigators located several ounces of methamphetamine packaged for resale, a loaded handgun, and other items indicative of drug distribution. The defendant has numerous prior felony convictions including fleeing officers, possession of cocaine with intent to deliver, grand theft, felony battery, aggravated stalking, possession of methamphetamine, possession of Lorazepam, felony domestic battery, and conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine. Sentencing is scheduled for January 22, 2027, at 11:00 am at the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before Chief United States District Judge Allen C. Winsor. Hinojosa faces up to life imprisonment. The case involved a joint investigation by the Tallahassee Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: Justice Department Sues to Stop Secret Gender Transitions at Anne Arundel County Public Schools
body: Press Release Justice Department Sues to Stop Secret Gender Transitions at Anne Arundel County Public Schools Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division announced today its lawsuit to stop Anne Arundel County Public Schools (AACPS) from secretly “gender transitioning” children without their parents’ knowledge or consent and blocking parents’ access to information about their children, which they are entitled to receive under federal law. The Department’s lawsuit enforces the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA). “Schools should not discuss preferred pronouns or ‘gender identity’ with a student without parental notification and consent,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Parents should not be lied to, stonewalled, or branded as ‘safety concerns’ when they ask to see the education records that reveal what schools are secretly doing to their children. This Department will end illegal school policies that keep parents in the dark.” The Department’s complaint alleges that AACPS’s gender policies deny parents their rights under FERPA and PPRA. AACPS directs school staff to solicit, document, and act upon a student’s self‑identified name, pronouns, and “gender identity” without notifying parents. AACPS designates “gender identity” information as “confidential” and instructs staff to withhold it from parents based on the unilateral and unfounded assertion that informing parents would pose a “safety concern” to students. AACPS reports “gender identity” information to the Maryland State Department of Education without parental notice or an opportunity to challenge its accuracy. The complaint also includes allegations about one anonymous family’s struggle with AACPS’s policies. During the 2025-2026 school year, AACPS questioned students, one-on-one, about their preferred names and pronouns. Thereafter, Jane and John Doe twice received emails from teachers referring to their daughter by a male name and pronouns. The Does confronted AACPS, but each time AACPS lied about helping their daughter pretend to be male at school. Although AACPS eventually admitting to lying, AACPS declined to give the Does details about their daughter’s “gender transition” and refused to turn over the child’s relevant education records. Today’s lawsuit is the latest in a series of steps taken by the Civil Rights Division to end public school policies that trample on parental rights guaranteed under FERPA and PPRA. FERPA authorizes parents to inspect and review their children’s education records, as well as correct or delete inaccurate information within those records. Under PPRA, parents have the right to give or withhold consent before schools collect sensitive personal information from minor students. Individuals may file FERPA and PPRA complaints with the U.S Department of Education at: studentprivacy.ed.gov/file-a-complaint . Note : Read the Department’s Complaint here Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1271

title: California Man Sentenced for Receiving Child Pornography and Transferring Obscene Material to a Minor
body: Press Release California Man Sentenced for Receiving Child Pornography and Transferring Obscene Material to a Minor Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Devin Ravine a/k/a “Derek Johnson,” age 21, of Riverside, California, was sentenced on October 22, 2026 by United States District Judge Anne M. Nardacci to 78 months of imprisonment, followed by 5 years of supervised release, for receiving child pornography and transferring obscene material to a minor.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. As part of his previous guilty plea, the defendant admitted that he contacted a 15-year-old child on a dating application, sent her pictures of his erect penis, and then directed her to produce sexually explicit video files. The victim complied, ultimately sending him a sexually explicit video of herself.  The victim came forward to law enforcement after FBI agents visited her school, which is located in the Capital Region, as part of its ongoing efforts to educate students about internet safety and sextortion. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III said: “This predator abused a 15-year-old girl in the Northern District of New York and was charged federally and brought back from California to face justice.  Had this predator been released to the California state courts, he would have likely been given a slap on the wrist.  This office has zero tolerance for child predators and abusers.  This defendant will be the guest of the federal penitentiary for the next 6 plus years.  I would like to commend the great investigative work of our FBI Albany Field office and the leadership of that office for bringing this case to light.” “Today, our thoughts are with the brave student who heard our message, recognized what was happening to her, and reported it to our team,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “We responded with the full of weight of the FBI and our incredible partnerships, and now Mr. Ravine is heading to federal prison for the next six and a half years. The FBI is deeply committed to continuing these conversations with our communities, and this investigation should prove just how quickly we will respond when someone comes forward. No matter where the predator is located, our Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force will use every resource necessary to track them down and send them to prison.” The FBI investigated the case with assistance from the FBI Riverside Field Office, the Riverside County District Attorney’s Office, and the Riverside County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Belliss prosecuted the case. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Nigerian Man Extradited from Benin to Face Federal Charges in $100 Million Stolen Identity Tax Scheme
body: Press Release Nigerian Man Extradited from Benin to Face Federal Charges in $100 Million Stolen Identity Tax Scheme Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA - Akinade Adedeji Raheem, a Nigerian citizen who allegedly conspired to file fraudulent tax returns seeking over $100 million in refunds using stolen identities, was arraigned yesterday on federal fraud, money laundering, and aggravated identity theft charges after his extradition from Benin. “Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other locations,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States, and his arrest confirms again that no alleged criminal can escape the reach of American justice.” “Raheem is an alleged co-conspirator in a nationwide identity theft scheme that victimized hundreds of taxpayers. The fraud also stole from the U.S. Treasury, impacting programs serving us all. These come with repercussions that are long lasting, which is why we place a global emphasis on arresting and extraditing these individuals,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr., of IRS-CI’s Texas Field Office. “Protect your tax returns with an identity protection pin at IRS.gov and know that we are pursuing financial criminals to take back the stolen money and their freedom.” “The investigative efforts of the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) and its partners, along with the prosecutorial work of the U.S. Attorney’s Office, demonstrate the commitment to pursuing, capturing, and prosecuting those who try to defraud the American people,” said TIGTA Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Colello. According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: Between 2018 and 2023, Raheem, who resided in Atlanta, and Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, conspired together and with others to claim fraudulent tax refunds using the stolen identities of accountants and American taxpayers. Over the course of their scheme, they allegedly filed more than 300 false tax returns claiming over $100 million in refunds from the IRS. Raheem, Eletu, and others allegedly obtained sensitive identifying information for tax professionals and taxpayers, including names, addresses, and Social Security numbers, by creating online accounts with the IRS and requesting private taxpayer information. Using the personal identifying information of others, Raheem, Eletu, and their co-conspirators allegedly filed tax returns claiming fraudulent refunds and then directed the IRS to split the refunds among prepaid debit cards shipped to addresses controlled by the co-conspirators. After the refunds were deposited onto the prepaid debit cards, Raheem and Eletu laundered some of the funds by purchasing, among other things, money orders in amounts low enough to avoid reporting thresholds. They also used the money orders to purchase used cars from auction sites, some of which they shipped to Nigeria, as well as designer clothing and other items. In April 2026, federal law enforcement agents sought to arrest Raheem at his residence and spoke to a man who identified himself as Raheem through a video doorbell and stated he was not home. Less than a week later, agents learned that Raheem booked a flight from Mexico City to Benin. On April 15, 2026, Raheem flew into Benin and was arrested by local authorities pursuant to an INTERPOL Red Notice. Last week, Benin authorities extradited Raheem to the United States, which was the second extradition to the United States from Benin in history. Yesterday, Akinade Adedeji Raheem, 43, of Nigeria, was arraigned on a federal indictment and detained in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending further proceedings. On February 24, 2026, a federal grand jury in the Northern District of Georgia indicted Raheem on one count of conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, 14 counts of access device fraud, and 14 counts of aggravated identity theft. Raheem faces maximum penalties of 20 years in prison for conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, 20 years for money laundering, and 10 years for access device fraud, as well as a mandatory sentence of two years for aggravated identity theft. On February 17, 2026, Eletu was indicted in the Western District of Texas. He was later arrested in the United Kingdom, where extradition proceedings are pending. Members of the public are reminded that the indictments only contain charges. The defendants are presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigations and TIGTA. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service provided significant assistance in this matter. The United States also thanks the United Kingdom for its valuable assistance in the investigation and INTERPOL’s National Central Bureau in Benin and Benin’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Ministry of Justice’s Office of Judiciary Cooperation; and Ministry of Interior, including the Directorate General of the Police Republicaine; the Airport Police; and the Police Special Operations Group for their valuable assistance in securing Raheem's arrest and extradition. Assistant United States Attorney Brian Pearce of the Northern District of Georgia, and Senior Litigation Counsel Michael C. Boteler and Trial Attorney Michael Jones of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section, are prosecuting the case. On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . title: Las Vegas woman sentenced to 15 years and 8 months in prison for role in drug mailing ring involving 83 pounds of methamphetamine
body: Press Release Las Vegas woman sentenced to 15 years and 8 months in prison for role in drug mailing ring involving 83 pounds of methamphetamine Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Ohio COLUMBUS, Ohio – A woman who participated in a large-scale operation involving the mailing of methamphetamine from California and Las Vegas to central Ohio was sentenced in U.S. District Court today to 188 months in prison. The government seized approximately 83 pounds of methamphetamine in this case. Tiauna Castro, 36, of Las Vegas, mailed drug packages from Las Vegas to Columbus. While this case was pending, Castro also committed more than half a million dollars in tax fraud. According to court documents, in April 2022, Castro and seven co-defendants were indicted for the drug conspiracy. The charges were the result of a 2021 investigation by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and the Central Ohio High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) Task Force. Investigators identified at least 128 mail parcels believed to contain methamphetamine. As part of the drug conspiracy, Castro met with bulk narcotics distributors and negotiated prices with the suppliers. She then bought bulk amounts of narcotics, stored them, repackaged them for shipping and sent them out through the U.S. Mail. Castro also committed tax fraud, filing false federal tax forms related to two sham businesses. She received more than $500,000 in refunds to which she was not entitled. She was charged with tax fraud in January 2025 while on pretrial release for the drug charges. Castro pleaded guilty in March 2026 to conspiring to distribute methamphetamine and submitting false claims. Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio, and Lesley Allison, Inspector in Charge, U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS),  announced the sentence imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Michael H. Watson. Assistant United States Attorneys Timothy D. Prichard and Emily Czerniejewski are representing the United States in this case. # # # Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Financial Fraud Tax Component USAO - Ohio, Southern
