title: Ukrainian National Sentenced for Role in Hacking Hospitals, Businesses, and Governments as Part of Ransomware Conspiracies Causing Over $100 Million in Losses
body: Press Release Ukrainian National Sentenced for Role in Hacking Hospitals, Businesses, and Governments as Part of Ransomware Conspiracies Causing Over $100 Million in Losses Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Artem Stryzhak, 36, a Ukrainian national, was sentenced today to 70 months in prison for conspiracy to commit computer fraud in connection with a series of ransomware attacks that targeted hospitals, government entities, law firms, and other businesses around the world. “This sentence concludes a years-long, multi-continent investigation into a defendant who participated in cyber-attacks against Americans’ businesses and health care,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Cybercriminals who terrorize American businesses cannot evade justice by operating from abroad or hiding behind sophisticated technology. Artem Stryzhak’s sentence underscores the Justice Department’s resolve to dismantle ransomware groups, hold them accountable, and protect American businesses and people from cyber extortion.” “Ransomware attacks like those committed by the defendant wreak enormous havoc — harming victim companies that pay millions in remediation and ransoms, preventing hospitals and other critical facilities from accessing data, and putting sensitive information in the hands of bad actors,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “Today’s sentence reflects that cybercriminals cannot hide from law enforcement and will face significant punishment for their criminal conduct. We remain determined to capture Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, a serial ransomware developer and Stryzhak’s co-conspirator.” “Disrupting a ransomware group that attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide and sentencing a defendant who had targeted healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic is of significant importance to this office,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe for the Middle District of Florida. “We are proud of our law enforcement partners for their skilled investigative work in bringing this criminal to justice.” “Artem Stryzhak is a prolific cybercriminal who worked with multiple ransomware groups to target U.S. businesses and hospitals,” said Operations Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Branch. “These groups disrupted patient care and caused more than $100 million in losses. Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak’s crimes and demonstrates the FBI’s global reach and extensive network of international partners. Multiple field offices contributed to this investigation, and our work does not end here. We will continue to leverage every tool at our disposal to track down Stryzhak’s co-conspirators and hold them accountable, including Volodymyr Viktorovych Tymoshchuk.” According to court documents, Stryzhak, formerly of Barcelona, Spain, conspired with others to perpetrate ransomware attacks on behalf of multiple ransomware groups against victim computer networks in the United States and other countries. The conspiracies caused significant damage to victim computer systems. Beginning in approximately June 2021, Stryzhak joined the ongoing Nefilim conspiracy as a Nefilim ransomware affiliate.  Stryzhak was given access to the Nefilim ransomware and agreed with one of the Nefilim ransomware group administrators, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, to pay the Nefilim administrators, including Tymoshchuk, 20% of the ransom proceeds extorted from victims in exchange for Stryzhak’s access to the Nefilim ransomware. The ransomware attacks that Stryzhak conducted with Nefilim ransomware included a June 2021 attack in which Stryzhak stole data from a company in the oil and gas transportation industry. About a week later, Stryzhak created email addresses that were incorporated in a ransom note sent to the victim company. Stryzhak conspired with the Nefilim ransomware actors until at least October 2021. If a victim paid the ransom demand, the perpetrators provided the decryption key, enabling the victim to decrypt files locked by the ransomware. Also according to court documents, Stryzhak separately joined the Hive ransomware group as one of its earliest affiliates. From June 2021 to January 2023, Hive conspirators attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide, including government entities, hospitals, and businesses. Hive ransomware attacks caused major disruptions in victim daily operations around the world and affected responses to the COVID-19 pandemic. In one case, a hospital attacked by the Hive ransomware group had to forgo digital technology to treat existing patients and was unable to accept new patients immediately following the attack. In his role as a Hive affiliate, Stryzhak and his co-conspirators deployed Hive ransomware against seven victims, including law firms, a dentist office, and a healthcare provider during the COVID-19 pandemic. Victims were unable to access their encrypted data. The FBI, as part of a months-long disruption campaign against the Hive ransomware group, provided a decryption key to one of Stryzhak’s victims, thereby allowing that victim to decrypt its encrypted data without having to pay a ransom. Stryzhak was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the United States in April 2025. Stryzhak pleaded guilty in December 2025 to two counts of conspiracy to commit fraud, extortion, and related activity in connection with computers. The FBI Springfield Field Office investigated the Nefilim ransomware case and the FBI Tampa Field Office investigated the Hive ransomware case. The Criminal Division’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI’s New York Field Office, and Spanish law enforcement authorities provided substantial assistance locating, arresting, and extraditing Stryzhak. Acting Assistant Deputy Chief James S. Yoon of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), former CCIPS Senior Trial Attorney Brian Z. Mund, and Assistant United States Attorneys Alexander F. Mindlin and Ellen H. Sise of the Eastern District of New York’s National Security and Cybercrime Section prosecuted the Nefilim ransomware case. CCIPS Trial Attorneys Alison M. Zitron and Christen M. Gallagher and Assistant United States Attorney Hannah Watson of the Middle District of Florida prosecuted the Hive ransomware case. The U.S. Department of State’s Transnational Organized Crime (TOC) Rewards Program has offered a reward of up to $11 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction or location of Stryzhak’s charged co-conspirator, Volodymyr Tymoshchuk. Anyone with information about Tymoshchuk should contact the FBI via phone at +1-917-242-1407, by email at TymoTips@fbi.gov , by contacting your local field office, if in the United States, or by contacting the nearest U.S. Embassy, if located overseas. More information about the Tymoshchuk TOC reward offer and one related to Hive ransomware is located on the State Department website. CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds. Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Cybercrime Components Criminal Division Criminal - Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Florida, Middle USAO - New York, Eastern Press Release Number: 26-1265
retained_feed_body: Artem Stryzhak, 36, a Ukrainian national, was sentenced today to 70 months in prison for conspiracy to commit computer fraud in connection with a series of ransomware attacks that targeted hospitals, government entities, law firms, and other businesses around the world.

American Woman Convicted of Receiving Military Training From ISIS in Syria
body: Press Release American Woman Convicted of Receiving Military Training From ISIS in Syria Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Defendant Received Training from the Khatiba Nusaybah, a Military Battalion Made Up of Female ISIS Members Today, a federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Halima Salman, 27, a U.S. citizen and former resident of Brooklyn, also known as “Umm Khattab al-Muhajir,” of receiving military-type training from the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS), a designated foreign terrorist organization, in Syria. Salman was convicted after a two-week trial before U.S. District Judge Natasha C. Merle. “The atrocities committed by ISIS, including mass executions, sexual slavery, and the systematic terrorizing of civilian populations, represent some of the gravest crimes of our time,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “There is simply no excuse for aligning with or receiving military training from an organization responsible for such suffering. Today's verdict sends a clear message that those who support this death cult will be found and prosecuted.” “With today’s verdict, Salman is held accountable for joining forces with a terrorist organization,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “ISIS ravaged Syria and caused havoc across the globe; our Office will continue to prosecute those who supported its murderous reign.” “It’s been nearly a decade since Halima Salman sought military training from ISIS in Syria, and today justice has been served,” said Assistant Director Jarod Brown of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division. “The FBI remains unwavering in its vigilance. We will continue to identify, disrupt, and bring to justice those who support foreign terrorist organizations and threaten the safety of our nation and our communities.” “Halima Salman knowingly sought out terrorist training from ISIS in Syria, she subscribed to their belief system and learned how to use weapons of mass violence,” said Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle of the FBI New York Field Office. “Defending the homeland will always be the top priority of the FBI, and anyone found guilty of supporting a Foreign Terrorist Organization will be investigated and prosecuted. Today’s verdict is a victory in the relentless fight against terrorism in the US.” As proven at trial, in September and October 2016, Salman’s parents traveled with her and her eight siblings out of the United States, ultimately destined for ISIS-controlled territory in Syria. In late 2016 or early 2017, Salman was 18 years old and married to an ISIS fighter in Syria, where she voluntarily sought military-type training and received authorization to carry ammunition and an assault rifle from ISIS. Salman received a document certifying that she successfully completed that training, a copy of which was found on her husband’s cellphone after it was recovered from the battlefield. Also on her husband’s device were photos depicting Salman with an ISIS flag in the background and a video that shows her brandishing an AK-47 rifle. The case was investigated by the FBI New York Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Adam Amir and Amanda Shami for the Eastern District of New York are prosecuting the case, with valuable assistance from Assistant U.S. Attorney Andrew Reich, Paralegal Specialist Emily Woodruff and Trial Attorney Patrick Cashman of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section. title: Scam Center Strike Force Expands Reach to Target Global Crime Syndicates; Charges Scammers Based in Africa and Tied to China
body: Press Release Scam Center Strike Force Expands Reach to Target Global Crime Syndicates; Charges Scammers Based in Africa and Tied to China Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia Scam Center Strike Force Expands Reach to Target Global Crime Syndicates; Charges Scammers Based in Africa and Tied to China 10.27.redacted_-_chui_kok_wa_et_al_affidavit.10.27-_redacted.pdf WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro, together with major federal law enforcement and in concert with interagency partners, announced actions taken by the Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force to secure America against cyber and cryptocurrency investment scams perpetrated by Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) groups. The Strike Force announced charges against six Africa-based scammers, with connections to Southeast Asia and China, which targeted Americans with fake Nonfungible Token (NFT) investment scams. U.S. Attorney Pirro also reviewed the Strike Force’s actions to date, noting that it had surpassed $1 billion in cryptocurrency restrained, and announced that the Strike Force has expanded its personnel and its reach to cover a global portfolio, following the expansion of Chinese connected TCOs to Africa and Europe. Joining in the announcement were U.S. Attorney Michael J. Heyman for the District of Alaska, Assistant Director Heith Janke of the FBI Criminal Division, and Special Agent in Charge Tara McLeese of the United States Secret Service (USSS) Washington Field Office. “Chinese TCOs are sending scammers into your dating network, your social network, and your messaging applications, all to steal Main Street America’s bank accounts. For the last year, the Strike Force has fought hard against the compounds in Southeast Asia facilitating these scammers, to the tune of $1 billion in cryptocurrency restrained,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “My Strike Force will expand and grow, and follow the scammers to Africa, India, Europe, and wherever they try to plant their operations. We will work with international partners to stop the cancerous spread of TCOs perpetrating scams on Americans.” As alleged in affidavits in support of an arrest of six individuals unsealed today, a criminal group with connections to Malaysia and China opened scam compounds in Madagascar in early 2025, likely having moved those operations from Cambodia after law enforcement action in that country. In the scheme, scammers posed as beautiful women who met victims on dating websites, eventually enlisting them to connect their cryptocurrency wallets to fraudulent websites associated with the NFT investments. Once connected, the scammers willed the victims to continue to fund their cryptocurrency wallets, and then surreptitiously pulled money from the victims’ wallets without their knowledge. Images of beautiful women, used by scammers to meet U.S. victims on dating sites. Instructions provided to human models (i.e., fake personas of a real person) to perpetrate the scheme. FBI investigators identified approximately 74 cryptocurrency wallets associated with victims in Maryland, Oregon, Nevada, and Minnesota who reported financial losses after interacting with fraudulent investment platforms online. The funds stolen from the victims were moved to cryptocurrency accounts associated with Chinese-based actors. Additionally unsealed today was a prior warrant wherein the government seized the websites associated with the scheme. Among the charges unsealed, Chui Kok Wa, was charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, as the leader of the NFT Scheme. Wa’s phones contained employment contracts, detailing overnight work schedules in Madagascar corresponding with daytime and evening hours in the United States, and providing employees with bonus payments tied to money stolen. Wa’s phones also included “scripts” or guides for what scammers should say to victims, which specifically told the workers that they were committing “an emotional scam, using the [victim’s] feelings for us to get him to invest.” Wa’s phone also had a roster that included the employees’ names, passport information, salary, hours, disciplinary actions taken against them, and a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the employees. “The defendants allegedly operated a sophisticated fraud scheme from Madagascar, exploiting the trust of Americans to steal their hard-earned money,” said U.S. Attorney Michael J. Heyman for the District of Alaska. “Operating from overseas does not place those who target Americans beyond the reach of U.S. law enforcement, and we will continue working with our domestic and international partners to aggressively hold those responsible accountable. I’m happy to be joining U.S. Attorney Pirro in collaborating and sharing the work on these important cases.” “Cybercriminals running scam centers wrongly assume they can relocate to escape our reach,” said Special Agent in Charge Tara McLeese of the U.S. Secret Service Washington Field Office. “Our agents and investigative analysts continue to show that these criminals can be identified, their money can be seized, and they can be held accountable.” “These scam compounds don’t stop at borders — they target Americans’ vulnerabilities and hard‑earned money,” said Assistant Director Heith Janke of the FBI Criminal Division. “The FBI, along with our partners at the Scam Center Strike Force, the Department of Justice, and the Secret Service have shown that there is no safe harbor for scammers who target Americans. We will hold you accountable and justice will find you.” Scammers kept track of their U.S. victims by listing their name, location, work, and other personal details in the Contact Cards on their phones. U.S. Attorney Pirro also noted that this case is emblematic of the spread of TCO actors from Asia spreading into other regions of the world. In August 2026, the FBI deployed a team to Madagascar at the invitation of the Madagascar Ministry of Justice and the Madagascar National Police (MNP) to assist MNP in the take down of 13 scam compounds and the more 3,200 electronic devices seized therein. After deploying, however, the U.S. government was stymied in efforts to interview the individuals involved, and Madagascar repatriated to China numerous suspects before the investigation was complete. Today, U.S. Attorney Pirro called on the Madagascar government to cooperate with the United States, extradite the six charged defendants, and further noted that the government had obtained a material witness warrant to interview 15 employees of the scheme, who claimed they were human trafficked and abused by Wa, but are believed to be held in jail in Madagascar. Also today, U.S. Attorney Pirro announced other actions taken by her Office in the last year, all related to efforts to protect Americans from scams and covered by President Trump’s Executive Order 14390—Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens: The Strike Force has restrained $1,006,460,156.82 in cryptocurrency-related fraud and scams. The Strike Force has seized 700 fraudulent crypto investment websites, shutting down pipelines used to lure victims. The Strike Force has seized Starlink terminals used by scam centers to maintain internet access. In fact, thousands of Starlink terminals have been taken down. The Strike Force conducted the first‑ever seizure of a Telegram channel used to recruit human trafficking victims into scam compounds. It also seized two additional Telegram channels hosting the Xinbi Guarantee Network, an illicit marketplace setup to provide websites and money laundering services that allows the scam centers to operate. The Strike Force, working with foreign partners, has seized and reviewed tens of thousands of devices used in scam compounds, to include computers, servers, hard drives and cell phones. The Strike Force, working in collaboration with private industry, had identified millions of scam accounts on U.S. networks. Meta reports that 17.3 million scam accounts have been deplatformed in the last year. The Strike Force is leading a national consumer awareness campaign, together with U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), FBI, and USSS. As part of that effort, the Strike Force has engaged the Ad Council Research Institute (ACRI), the research arm of the nonprofit Ad Council. ACRI’s study will examine how scammers target Americans, especially older adults, and which messages are most likely to help people recognize and avoid fraud. ACRI will share its findings over the coming months to guide the development of the Strike Force’s campaign. The U.S. Attorney's Office for DC along with U.S. Secret Service and the South African Police Service worked together to charge a prolific sextortionist, Ifeel Simango, in South Africa. Simango is charged with extorting at least 54 victims using sexually explicit images of them, including one victim in Switzerland who committed suicide as a result of the scheme. Simango now faces 52 charges in South Africa, including fraud, money laundering, child sexual abuse, and murder. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia, along with the U.S. Secret Service and the Nigerian Police Force – National Cyber Crime Center (NCCC), and pursuant to an investigative referral from Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit, arrested three key players alleged to be responsible for a global cybercrime conspiracy to manufacture and sell illegal “phishing” kits.  These kits facilitated business email compromise, ransomware, and financial fraud targeting hospitals within the American health care industry, and victims around the world resulting in the theft of at least 5,000 credentials from 94 countries, and the disruption of critical surgical care. The phishing kit, named RaccoonO365, provided criminals with a means to mimic official Microsoft communications and branding to steal credentials from users of Microsoft's infrastructure (i.e. Outlook.com). By giving criminals a pathway to gain access to American citizens’ inboxes, the kits enabled a range of illicit activity, including business email compromise, social engineering fraud, and other cybercrime. The Strike Force appreciates the work of Microsoft, Meta, Google, Tether, TRM, Elliptic, Chainalysis, Infoblox, and Block6IQ, who have provided voluntary assistance on specific matters announced today. U.S. Attorney Pirro also announced today that OpenAI has committed to working with the Strike Force to counter this threat. ********************************************** About the Scam Center Strike Force The Scam Center Strike Force was officially launched by U.S. Attorney Pirro in November 2025 to address the growing threat posed by Chinese organized crime syndicates operating scam centers primarily in Southeast Asia. The Strike Force targets cryptocurrency investment fraud, cyber-enabled fraud, human trafficking, and money laundering operations that have cost American victims billions of dollars. According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), cyber-enabled fraud schemes were responsible for almost 85% of all losses reported to IC3 in 2025. Within that category, CIF schemes have continued to grow, and the IC3 calculated the reported losses from CIF scams rose, from $4.57 billion in 2023, to $8.65 billion in 2025, an increase of 89%. These figures, largely based on losses reported by victims, likely significantly under-represent the true loss amounts incurred by Americans, since most fraud victims do not report to IC3, if at all. On March 6, 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order directing the Administration to prioritize cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes draining American families of their life savings. Through the Executive Order, President Trump is unleashing every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cyber-enabled fraud. The Scam Center Strike Force is a critical node in executing the mission outlined in the President’s Order. Founded by the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, the Strike Force has been joined it its work by the FBI, the U.S. Secret Service, Justice Department’s Criminal Division, the USPIS, IRS Criminal Investigation, and Homeland Security Investigations-D.C. and Colorado Springs, as well as the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Alaska, Hawaii, Eastern North Carolina, Rhode Island, and Western Washington. The Strike Force works in collaboration with other federal agencies, including the Treasury and State Departments, and coordinates with the National Coordination Center (NCC) and Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF). The Strike Force works in strategic partnership with private industry and calls on all U.S. businesses to take more proactive steps to protect users from scam operations. The Scam Center Strike Force will use every tool available to help secure Main Street Americans from these scams. With its interagency and public partners, it will educate Americans on how to identify these scams, prevent generational wealth from flowing from America into the pockets of Chinese organized crime, and work with unwavering focus to return stolen funds to victims. Assistant U.S. Attorney (AUSA) Karen P. Seifert for the District of Columbia directs the Strike Force. The Madagascar case is handled by AUSA Seifert and AUSA Mac Caille Petursson of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Alaska, along with the FBI’s Honolulu Field Office. The cryptocurrency seizure team is led by DC AUSA Rick Blaylock. From the U.S. Secret Service, these cryptocurrency seizure matters are handled by the Global Investigative Operation Center and Field Offices in San Francisco, San Diego, Memphis, Washington D.C., Nashville and Seattle Field Offices. From the FBI, these cryptocurrency seizure matters are handled by the Cyber Enabled Fraud and Money Laundering Unit and Field Offices in Washington D.C., San Francisco, Memphis, Honolulu, Phoenix, San Diego, New York City and Chattanooga. The website seizures were handled by both FBI and USSS, including through the work of the Level Up Initiative. The Simango case was handled by D.C. AUSAs Matthew Kahn, Jason Facci, and Caroline Burrell along with U.S. Secret Service’s Johannesburg Field Office and the South African National Prosecuting Authority. The RaccoonO365 case is being handled by D.C. AUSAs Matthew Kahn and Jason Facci, along with the U.S. Secret Service Pretoria Resident Office and the U.S. Secret Service Criminal Investigative Division. The Office of International Affairs, the U.S. Department of State, the Legal Attaches for South Africa & Madagascar, Thailand, and Cambodia, the South African Police Service, the Nigerian Police Force, and the National Prosecuting Authority of Switzerland all provided substantial assistance related to cases announced today. ********************************************** (Below) Wa’s phones also included “scripts” and instructional guides for what scammers should say to victims, which specifically told the workers that they were committing “an emotional scam, using the [victim’s] feelings for us to get him to invest.” Scammers instructed U.S. victims how to connect their cryptocurrency wallet to the scam website, where thereafter the scammers pulled out the fund unbeknownst to the victims. Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Fraud National Security Components Asset Forfeiture Program Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Alaska USAO - District of Columbia

Federal Jury Convicts Registered Sex Offender for Child Sex Crimes
body: Press Release Federal Jury Convicts Registered Sex Offender for Child Sex Crimes Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – William Jared Breski, 38, of Eastpoint, Florida, was found guilty by a federal jury of attempting to entice a minor to produce child pornography, attempting to transfer obscene material to a minor, and a penalty for registered sex offenders. The verdict was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “My office takes seriously its duty to protect the most vulnerable members of our community against predators, like this defendant, who would seek to sexually exploit and victimize them, and this successful prosecution will ensure he is kept behind federal bars where he belongs and away from our kids. I appreciate the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners that supported this trial success, and my office remains committed to aggressively prosecuting these crimes to keep our kids safe.” Trial testimony revealed that in July 2025, local law enforcement conducted an undercover operation to identify and apprehend registered sex offenders who were in violation of state registration requirements. During the operation, an undercover law enforcement officer contacted the defendant’s social media account, which he had failed to disclose as a required in his previous sex offender registration forms. After being informed he was speaking to a 15-year-old child, the defendant expressed an interest in talking to the child about sex. Ten days later, following his release from jail on state criminal charges, the defendant re-initiated contact with the undercover officer posing as the child and sent numerous unsolicited images of himself nude. He then encouraged the “child” to produce sexually explicit images for him to view. The defendant has been a registered sex offender since 2021. Breski faces a mandatory minimum 10 years’ imprisonment, and up to life imprisonment, on the attempted enticement count; up to 10 years’ imprisonment on the attempted transmission of obscene material count; and 10 years’ imprisonment consecutive to any other sentence imposed on the penalties for registered sex offender count. The case involved a joint investigation by the Leon County Sheriff’s Office and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant United States Attorney Emma Schwan is prosecuting the case. Sentencing is scheduled for January 28, 2027, at 2:00 pm at the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Robert L. Hinkle. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . Contact United States Attorney’s Office Northern District of Florida USAFLN.Press.Office@usdoj.gov X: @USAO_NDFL Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Northern

title: Northern Nevada Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Embezzling Nearly $8 Million From a Federal Grant Project
body: Press Release Northern Nevada Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Embezzling Nearly $8 Million From a Federal Grant Project Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A northern Nevada business owner pleaded guilty today to embezzling more than $7.8 million from “The Lovelock Project,” a federally-funded high-speed internet construction project near Lovelock, Nevada, to his personal bank account. “Stealing public funds intended to connect rural communities is a direct assault on the taxpayers of Nevada,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “When individuals treat federal grants as personal piggy banks and hide stolen millions in cryptocurrency, they undermine public trust and rob citizens of critical infrastructure. I commend our Nevada State Director at USDA, Alida Ceballos, for the continued partnership with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and helping ensure that anyone who defrauds government programs can be aggressively pursued.” "Through multiple fraudulent schemes, the defendant clearly exploited trust to line his pockets,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “The grants were intended to enhance broadband infrastructure in rural communities in Nevada. Instead, the defendant brazenly misappropriated these funds for personal gain. Today’s guilty plea ensures he will finally be held fully accountable for exploiting public resources to fund his private lifestyle." “Fighting waste, fraud, and abuse is essential to our mission at USDA Rural Development, and we are proud to support the Vice President’s Pledge to protect Americans from fraud,” said Nevada State Director Alida Ceballos for USDA Rural Development. “This plea would not have happened without an all-of-government approach to tackling fraud, and I am deeply thankful to the leadership of First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah and our partners at DOJ, USDA OIG, and the FBI for their partnership and support for rural Nevada.” According to court documents, Stephen A. Kromer owned Uprise, LLC, a former internet service provider located in Reno, Nevada. In 2022, the United States Department of Agriculture (“USDA”) awarded Uprise a $27 million federal grant to construct a high-speed broadband network in rural Lovelock, Nevada, about 100 miles northeast of Reno. The grant was funded by the ReConnect Program, a federal program that promoted the construction of high-speed internet networks in under-utilized rural areas across the United States. As a condition to receiving the federal grant, Uprise agreed to contribute approximately $9 million toward the cost of the Lovelock project. Uprise obtained this money from the State of Nevada and deposited it into a separate financial account designated solely for the Lovelock Project and overseen by the USDA From May 2024 through November 2024, Kromer embezzled more than $7.8 million from the ReConnect Program by transferring the money from the designated account to his personal bank account and falsely accounting for the transfers as expenditures for the Lovelock project. The Indictment alleged that Kromer then laundered the embezzled money by subsequently moving the embezzled proceeds from his personal bank account into accounts he held at various cryptocurrency exchanges where the money was converted into cryptocurrency. Kromer pleaded guilty to one count of federal money laundering. Sentencing is scheduled for March 9, 2027, before United States District Judge Richard F. Boulware II. At sentencing, Kromer faces the maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison. title: American Woman Convicted of Receiving Military Training from ISIS in Syria
body: Press Release American Woman Convicted of Receiving Military Training from ISIS in Syria Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York The Defendant Received Training from the Nusaybah Katiba, a Military Battalion Made Up of Female ISIS Members BROOKLYN, NY – Today, a federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Halima Salman, also known as “Umm Khattab al-Muhajir,” of receiving military-type training from the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) in Syria.  Salman, a U.S. citizen and former resident of Brooklyn, was convicted after a seven-day trial before United States District Judge Natasha C. Merle. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, John A. Eisenberg, Assistant Attorney General for the Justice Department’s National Security Division, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the verdict. “With today’s verdict, Salman is held accountable for joining forces with a terrorist organization,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “ISIS ravaged Syria and caused havoc across the globe; our Office will continue to prosecute those who supported its murderous reign.” Mr. Nocella expressed his appreciation to the U.S. Special Operations Command, the U.S. Department of the Army, the U.K. Ministry of Defense, the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI’s National Security & Cyber Law Branch, the U.S. Department of War Office of the General Counsel, and the U.S. Department of State for their assistance. “The atrocities committed by ISIS, including mass executions, sexual slavery, and the systematic terrorizing of civilian populations, represent some of the gravest crimes of our time,” stated Assistant Attorney General Eisenberg. “There is simply no excuse for aligning with or receiving military training from an organization responsible for such suffering. Today’s verdict sends a clear message that those who support this death cult will be found and prosecuted.” “Halima Salman knowingly sought out terrorist training from ISIS in Syria, she subscribed to their belief system and learned how to use weapons of mass violence.  Defending the homeland will always be the top priority of the FBI, and anyone found guilty of supporting a Foreign Terrorist Organization will be investigated and prosecuted. Today’s verdict is a victory in the relentless fight against terrorism in the U.S.,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. As proved at trial, in September and October 2016, Salman’s parents traveled with her and her eight siblings out of the United States, ultimately destined for ISIS-controlled territory in Syria. Following her July 2017 marriage to an ISIS fighter in Syria, Salman, then 18 years old, voluntarily sought military-type training and received authorization to carry an assault rifle from ISIS, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization.  Salman received a document certifying that she successfully completed that training, a copy of which was found on her husband’s cellphone after it was recovered from the battlefield.  Also on her husband’s device were photos depicting Salman, including one image with an ISIS flag in the background, as well as a video that shows her brandishing an AK-47 rifle. The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and Cybercrime Section.  Assistant United States  Attorneys Amanda Shami and Adam Amir are in charge of the prosecution, with valuable assistance from Assistant United States Attorney Andrew Reich, Paralegal Specialist Emily Woodruff, and Trial Attorney Patrick Cashman of the U.S. Department of Justice’s National Security Division, Counterterrorism Section. The Defendant : HALIMA SALMAN (also known as “Umm Khattab al-Muhajir”) Age: 27 Woodstock, New Hampshire E.D.N.Y. title: Gainesville Woman Convicted in $8.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Gainesville Woman Convicted in $8.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal jury in the Middle District of Florida convicted a Florida woman who owned a durable medical equipment (DME) company and managed several other DME companies for her role in a fraud scheme that took advantage of the elderly and disabled and caused the submission of over $8.6 million in fraudulent claims to Medicare. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Sophie Dufort, 57, of Gainesville, Florida, conspired with Paula Pirone, 70, of Ocala, Florida, and others to submit fraudulent claims to Medicare based on fake doctors’ prescriptions for orthotic braces. Dufort and her co-conspirators illegally purchased these prescriptions from purported marketing companies that engaged in high pressure and manipulative telemarketing calls to get Medicare beneficiaries’ information. When confronted with complaints that the voice on purported call recordings did not match the beneficiaries’ voice, one co-conspirator explained that “some of the calls from overseas would be faked” and used to justify a bogus prescription. The marketing companies then paid medical practitioners to sign prescriptions for orthotic braces without contacting or evaluating the patients, or stole doctor’s credentials to create forged prescriptions, and then sold those prescriptions to Dufort’s and her co-conspirators’ DME companies. Dufort and her co-conspirators then shipped braces to the Medicare beneficiaries and billed Medicare for millions of dollars in claims, despite the fact that the beneficiaries did not want or need the braces and no doctor had examined the beneficiary to determine if they needed the braces. And, as one medical expert testified, use of these combinations of braces could be “very dangerous” for the elderly Medicare population. When people complained and wanted to return the braces, “they would just tell [them] to just get rid of them or . . . just pass them down” so Dufort and her co-conspirators would not have to pay Medicare back. The defendant was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, two counts of health care fraud, one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States and to offer and pay illegal kickbacks, and one count of offering and paying illegal kickbacks.  Dufort faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison for conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, 10 years in prison for each health care fraud count and kickback count, and 5 years in prison for conspiracy to defraud the United States and to offer and pay illegal kickbacks.  A sentencing hearing is scheduled in Jan. 2027.  A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and Middle District of Florida U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. The case was investigated by the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Trial Attorney Jody King of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney William Hamilton for the Middle District of Florida are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1267

title: “Bulletproof” website domain seized in international law enforcement operation
body: Press Release “Bulletproof” website domain seized in international law enforcement operation Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia ALEXANDRIA, Va. – Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, and Darren B. Cox, Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI Washington Field Office, announced today the seizure of the website virtualine.net after it was used to commit and facilitate prolific criminal activity, including the advertisement of sexually explicit images of minors, the intentional disclosure of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions of adults and minors, and international money laundering designed to conceal and promote criminal conduct. According to court records, the United States obtained court authorization to seize virtualine.net, which is the website for Virtualine, aka Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech.  Virtualine is a “bulletproof” service offering hosting and server solutions with domain name purchasing options. Virtualine advertises its services to criminals on cybercrime forums. For example, in September 2024, Virtualine told a user on Exploit.in: “You can use Virtualine for all illegal/black hat activities (including phis[h]ing, carding, email spam, port scanning and all others) except for child contents and terrorism activities.” In March 2026, Virtualine advertised its “additional protection plan,” which it offered to its customers after “receiv[ing] an official request from law enforcement agencies.” Under this plan, Virtualine would move the customer’s criminal infrastructure to “another shell company not affiliated with Virtualine, after which the server is reactivated.” As Virtualine advertised to users on the platform HackForums in June 2025, “Virtualine ignored more abuse than your last three therapists.” Despite advertising that it does not allow “child contents” on its server, Virtualine knowingly hosted a website that did so, identified in court records as Vendor 1. Vendor 1 is a criminal online forum that allows users to post and sell access to nude, sexually suggestive, and/or sexually explicit images and videos of minors and adults. Vendor 1 also promotes a hack-for-hire service in which users can pay hackers to access victims’ online accounts without their consent and illicitly obtain explicit images and videos. In January 2026, about one month after Virtualine assigned an IP address to Vendor 1, Virtualine began receiving notifications about sexually explicit images and videos of minors on that server. Despite receiving numerous notices from law enforcement in Germany, Canada, and Australia; the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) in the United States; and even from a victim’s attorney, Virtualine continued to host Vendor 1’s services. Furthermore, Virtualine worked closely with Vendor 1 to create a new website where Vendor 1’s clients could upload their illicit content and from which they downloaded it when they made a purchase. Virtualine hosts this new website to this day, and it has already received at least one abuse complaint about sexually explicit images of children found on that website. Virtualine.net included a number of payment options for Virtualine’s customers, including Vendor 1. Virtualine accepted payment through BTC [NO-AML], specific unhosted bitcoin addresses that allowed customers to direct pay without concern their funds would be flagged as illicit. The funds Virtualine’s criminal customers paid to Virtualine, some of which can be traced directly to various criminal groups, were received by Virtualine and then further laundered to conceal the origin of the funds. This case was investigated by the FBI Washington Field Office with significant assistance from Germany’s Polizei Hessen, the Netherlands’ Politie Midden-Nederland, the U.K.’s National Crime Agency, and private sector partners OverRIPE and Lumen. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs provided significant assistance. The government is represented by Assistant United States Attorneys Laura D. Withers and Stefanie A. Schwartz in these matters. Contact USAVAE.Press@usdoj.gov Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Cybercrime Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Virginia, Eastern

title: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer
body: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer Oct 26, 2026 | Amy Coleman - Executive Vice President, Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees today. Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs. The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program. What employees should know This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below . This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs. Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours. Looking ahead The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute. My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving. Thank you for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another. Amy This Viva Engage post has been edited slightly for external use.

title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026)
body: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026) A few weeks ago I presented to a small group of commercial and technology leaders from Brazilian agribusiness at the AWS office in São Paulo. My talk ran through where generative AI fits across the different stages of an agribusiness operation, and the point I kept returning to is that the markets we call traditional are exactly the ones where keeping up with this technology decides who ends up ahead of the curve. Nobody there was arguing about whether AI belongs in agriculture. The questions were about delivery: who receives the output, in which language, on which device, often while driving between farms. That is why a launch I might otherwise have filed under routine leads my list this week. The Amazon Polly Generative engine upgrade added 14 new voices, two of them in Brazilian Portuguese. When your user has both hands on a steering wheel, the interface is a voice. Presenting “GenAI no Agronegócio Brasileiro” at the AWS office in São Paulo. The rest of the week had a sharper edge. The biggest launch is a security service built on the premise that the gap between a vulnerability being disclosed and a vulnerability being exploited has effectively closed, and AWS published the honeypot evidence for exactly that in the same week. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available AWS Continuum reframes vulnerability management as an end-to-end job rather than a scanner that hands you a list. It builds a context graph from your repositories and your AWS environment, assigns each finding an evidence level, and reproduces exploitable findings in an isolated sandbox with proof-of-concept code so you see the issue rather than a severity label. It ranks issues by how close the attack path runs to business-critical systems, then opens the fix as a pull request. The control boundary matters: every remediation currently requires human approval, so you review and merge the pull request, with autonomous classes of fix gated behind confidence thresholds for the future. The “why now” came from AWS’s own honeypots in the same week. Amazon Threat Intelligence found a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry dated October 17, four days before CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were publicly disclosed, and on disclosure day proof-of-concept exploits were circulating around 02:00 UTC, roughly twelve hours before the embargo was due to lift at 14:00 UTC. The practical reading is direct: a patch window measured in days assumes a delay that no longer exists, and an investigation should start from the earliest known exploitation rather than from the disclosure date. AWS also published the AWS WAF mitigations for the same CVEs. Continuum is available in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon). Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway Amazon ECS Gateway splits the work of exposing a service between the people who own the network and the people who own the application. Platform teams define one gateway with the organization’s subnets, security groups, TLS certificates, listener settings, and AWS WAF web ACLs. Application teams opt in by adding a gateway connector to the service definition, and ECS gives them an ACM certificate, a unique DNS hostname, listener rules, a target group, and a security group that admits traffic only from the Application Load Balancer. The numbers make the economics clear: up to 25 services share a single ALB, ECS provisions the first ALB on first connect and removes ALBs when they are no longer needed, and a gateway can associate with up to 10,000 clusters, with five gateways per cluster. You can adopt it incrementally with UpdateService while your existing load balancer stays in place. Amazon ECS Gateway is available in all commercial Regions where Amazon ECS is available, at no additional charge. Last week’s launches Here are some launches that caught my attention this week. Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine – The Generative engine now runs a larger, more expressive catalog: 57 generative voices across 11 languages and 25 locales, with 14 new voices across 9 locales and Hindi and Finnish generally available for the first time. Two of the new voices are Brazilian Portuguese, Leo and Carolina. It is a drop-in upgrade, so the voice names, the same SynthesizeSpeech call, and the price all stay the same while the output gets more natural. AWS announces TorchNeuron: native PyTorch support for AWS Trainium (public beta) – TorchNeuron is an open source PyTorch backend that lets you run your model on Trainium by switching to .to(‘neuron’), a configuration change instead of a rewrite, with eager execution and torch.compile intact. It integrates with the Neuron Kernel Interface for custom operators, and it works on Trainium2 and Trainium3 instances. If you want the bigger picture on why hardware choice should not lock in your software, the AWS Insights piece on that theme is a good companion read, and the release lands alongside AWS Neuron 2.33 . New ways to customize models with Amazon SageMaker AI, without managing GPUs – Training sessions are now generally available, giving you control of the post-training loop, including custom loss functions and reward signals, while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, distributed execution, fault recovery, and checkpoint storage. You pay for the tokens SageMaker AI processes, and the meter stops while your reward function scores a batch. There is a full technical walkthrough , the training session APIs , and new support for Muse Glimmer, Qwen 3.8, and Ministral 3 . Structured outputs for Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock – You can now get schema-compliant JSON back from any Anthropic Claude model on Amazon Bedrock, across both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing. That makes jobs like pulling every required field from a financial report, parsing clinical notes, or routing support tickets by intent far more reliable to automate. Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration with zero downtime – You can migrate self-managed Valkey or Redis OSS on Amazon EC2 into ElastiCache Serverless with zero downtime, meaning zero errors returned to the client during the move, measured the way the ElastiCache SLA measures availability. You prepare the migration, start the data sync, then choose a manual or automatic cutover, with no third-party replication tools. It is available in all commercial Regions, the China Regions, and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Other AWS news Here are some additional projects and posts that you might find interesting. Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry – AWS Agent Registry is a managed catalog for MCP servers, agents, and agent skills, so an orchestrator can search approved capabilities at runtime instead of compiling every tool in at build time. This walkthrough shows the discover, instantiate, and execute loop in a working sample, with search results that return connection metadata but never invocation credentials. Tokenomics for coding agents: benchmark cost and quality on your own code – Coding assistants replay a growing transcript on every turn, so their cost math is nothing like ordinary inference. This post gives you open source tooling to measure model, harness, and hosting choices on your own repositories and build a cost-and-quality frontier you own, with sample results where routing came out 44.7 percent cheaper for 4.8 percent lower mean quality. How U.S. Bank migrated 119 TB from Oracle Exadata to Amazon RDS for Oracle – U.S. Bank moved four Oracle Exadata databases totaling about 119 TB to Amazon RDS for Oracle using a config-driven pipeline built on Oracle XTTS, AWS DataSync, and Amazon EFS. The initial baseline copy finished in about 7 days with zero data loss and cutovers averaging roughly four hours per database, over a bandwidth-capped Direct Connect link. Upcoming AWS events Mark your calendars for these upcoming events. AWS re:Invent – AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas, with more than 2,200 sessions. The session catalog is live and reserved seating is open, so now is the time to build your schedule. AWS Community Days – AWS Community Day Brasil Norte takes place in Belém on October 31, closing out the 2026 Brazilian community season. Check the hub for events near you. That’s all for this week. Check back next Monday for another Weekly Roundup! – Daniel This post is part of our Weekly Roundup series. Check back each week for a quick roundup of interesting news and announcements from AWS!

title: Final Defendants Plead Guilty in $65 Million Multinational Fraud Ring Targeting Thousands of Seniors
body: Press Release Final Defendants Plead Guilty in $65 Million Multinational Fraud Ring Targeting Thousands of Seniors Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO –  The last of 25 defendants in a $65 million fraud scheme that preyed on thousands of elderly victims in San Diego and beyond admitted their crimes on Friday, marking a significant step toward accountability in the sprawling international case that was bolstered by YouTube scambaiters. The 25 defendants – mostly Chinese nationals – were arrested in August 2025 after a nationwide, weeklong takedown in California, New York, Texas and Michigan. Three charged defendants remain fugitives. Haotian Zhang and Zetian Zhang pleaded guilty in federal court on Friday. Haotian Zhang, a Chinese national, was remanded into custody by U.S. District Judge Todd W. Robinson following his guilty plea. Over the past few months, eight other defendants charged as part of the investigation—Guangli Lin, Cheng Li, Weining Su, aka “Ning Ma,” Hongsen Cao, Xinyu Shao, Renchao Chen, Dexiao Lin, Zhiyi Zhang—have also pleaded guilty in federal court for their roles in the same fraud and money laundering scheme, and two defendants—Huajian Chen and Jianhao Gao—recently pleaded guilty to operating an unlicensed money transmission business. Videos by YouTubers from Scammer Payback and Trilogy Media helped law enforcement identify multiple defendants and uncover the structure of the fraud conspiracy.  Indeed, in their respective plea agreements, defendants Zhiyi Zhang and Huajian Chen, shown below, admitted to being in YouTube videos in which they were confronted about their involvement in the charged criminal activity. Operating since at least 2019 and rooted in Southern California, the criminal network—primarily composed of Chinese nationals, many in the U.S. illegally—worked closely with India-based scam call centers. Fraudsters who took the calls posed as technical support agents, government officials, or bank employees, according to court records. Once a victim had been defrauded, victims were instructed to withdraw bulk cash, to conceal the cash in packages, and to send cash-laden packages via express mail carriers to names and addresses provided by the conspirators. The recipient names were fictitious names corresponding with fake IDs. The recipient addresses were for the short-term rental locations. In their respective plea agreements, defendants admitted that to facilitate receipt of victim packages, members of the conspiracy booked short-term rentals in a hub-and-spoke pattern: a hub would be booked for approximately one week; spoke locations would be booked nearby for shorter stays.  After some time, members of the conspiracy would relocate to a new location and continue the pattern. In August 2025, federal agents coordinated a sweeping nationwide takedown of the investigation, including arrests in Southern California, Texas, Michigan and New York.  The investigation started in December 2020 after an elderly victim contacted an express mail carrier after being defrauded into sending bulk cash in the mail. That led to the discovery of 11 total packages, containing approximately $135,000 in cash.  Each of the packages was addressed to a fake name and a short-term rental in the San Diego area. The investigation also led to the discovery of several YouTube videos posted in 2020 and 2021 that helped identify other members of the conspiracy. YouTuber Pierogi from “Scammer Payback”— which is known for exposing scammers—documented his interaction with the India-based scam call centers.  In a series of videos, Pierogi from Scammer Payback teamed up with two other YouTubers from “Trilogy Media” to publish videos on their respective YouTube channels. In coordinated sting operations, Scammer Payback and Trilogy Media baited fraudsters, confronted them on camera, and published those videos to their respective YouTube channels. Videos posted in 2020 and 2021 helped law enforcement identify Zhiyi Zhang, Dudu Chen and Huajian Chen. The videos also helped shed light on how the conspiracy operated and led to the identification of high-level members of the organization. After defrauding victims, members of the conspiracy also laundered the proceeds of the fraud scheme.  Specifically, members of the conspiracy set up the operation to conceal the fact that the cash-laden packages were obtained through fraud. Members of the conspiracy also used the proceeds of the fraud scheme to pay other members of the conspiracy and to compensate them for travel expenses used to further the fraud scheme. Sentencing hearings for each of the defendants are scheduled before U.S. District Judge Todd W. Robinson as set forth below. title: Reno Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Prison for Drug Trafficking Conspiracy
body: Press Release Reno Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Prison for Drug Trafficking Conspiracy Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada RENO – A northern Nevada man was sentenced today by United States District Judge Miranda M. Du to 188 months in prison for his role in a conspiracy to possess and distribute methamphetamine. The government recommended life in prison. “This defendant chose to flood our communities with pure poison for profit, completely indifferent to the lives he ruined and the families he tore apart,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “A sentence of 188 months ensures that his career as a poison peddler is officially over, and it serves as a stark warning to anyone else thinking they can operate a drug conspiracy: we will hunt you down, dismantle your network, and lock you away where you can no longer harm the public.” “Methamphetamine and fentanyl remain at the forefront of the drug crisis devastating Americans,” said David Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada. “Drug criminals continue to exploit our communities for profit despite the severe harm they cause. Today's sentencing reinforces our unyielding commitment to holding offenders accountable and securing justice. DEA stands united with our federal partners to protect the health and safety of our communities.” According to court documents, from December 16, 2022, to June 19, 2023, Max Vaneeten operated a drug trafficking organization based in Fallon, Nevada. He conspired with co-defendants Tasia Ratti and Chace Young to possess and distribute large quantities of crystal methamphetamine through the greater Nevada area. On June 18, 2023, Vaneeten was stopped in California. Law enforcement found methamphetamine, cocaine, and cash. In total, about one pound of cocaine and about 35 pounds of methamphetamine were distributed during the drug trafficking conspiracy. Vaneeten pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute a controlled substance, two counts of distribution of a controlled substance, and one count of possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance. Ratti was sentenced to 97 months in prison and Young was sentenced to 87 months in prison. The DEA investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Melinda Brewer prosecuted the case. ### Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Nevada

title: Armed Meth Dealer Faces Life in Prison in Operation Take Back America Case
body: Press Release Armed Meth Dealer Faces Life in Prison in Operation Take Back America Case Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Georgia High‑Purity Meth, Stolen Firearm, Drug Distribution Site Found in Columbus Investigation COLUMBUS, Ga. – A Columbus resident is facing up to life in prison for distributing methamphetamine in the city, the result of an Operation Take Back America investigation conducted by federal, state, and local law enforcement in the community. Demetric Thomas, aka “Meatball,” 38, of Columbus, pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of methamphetamine before U.S. District Judge Clay Land on October 26. Thomas faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years up to a maximum of life in prison, to be followed by five years of supervised release, and a maximum $10 million fine. The sentencing date will be determined by the Court. There is no parole in the federal system. “This case reflects the continued results of our coordinated efforts to hold armed drug traffickers accountable in Columbus and across the Middle District of Georgia,” said U.S. Attorney William R. ‘Will’ Keyes. “Through Operation Take Back America, our office and our law enforcement partners are dismantling the networks that fuel violence and threaten community safety.” “Methamphetamine trafficking puts our communities at risk, particularly when drug distributors operate alongside stolen firearms and other dangerous drugs,” said Thomas Clark, Senior Supervisory Special Agent from FBI Atlanta’s Columbus office. “The FBI and our partners remain committed to disrupting drug trafficking networks and holding dangerous offenders accountable.” “This case demonstrates our ongoing efforts to target armed drug traffickers causing havoc in the Middle District of Georgia,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “Working alongside our law enforcement partners, we are committed to disrupting drug trafficking operations and protecting the communities we serve.” “Drugs such as methamphetamine endanger lives and leave lasting damage in families and communities,” said GBI Director Chris Hosey. “Collaborative law enforcement efforts like Operation Take Back America are vital to disrupting drug trafficking. Georgians deserve safe, drug-free communities, and we remain committed to purging these dangerous substances from our streets.” “This type of illegal drug activity has no place in Columbus. The distribution of dangerous drugs puts our community at risk, and we will not tolerate it,” said Columbus Police Chief Stoney Mathis. “We will continue working with our law enforcement partners to identify those responsible and put an end to their operations.” According to court documents, agents with the FBI, DEA, GBI, and the Columbus Police Department were investigating drug trafficking in Columbus. On May 21, 2025, federal and state law enforcement conducted a controlled drug purchase using a confidential source, purchasing 111.2 grams of 98% pure methamphetamine from Thomas at 2318 6 th Avenue in Columbus. Agents conducted a second controlled purchase of methamphetamine from Thomas at the same location on Oct. 14, 2025, buying 97.2 grams of 93% pure methamphetamine from the defendant. On Oct. 22, 2025, the FBI, DEA, GBI, and CPD executed a search warrant at the 6th Avenue location.  Thomas was there and fled as officers approached but was ultimately taken into custody after a brief pursuit. Officers found $3,337 in cash on Thomas, along with nearly 90 grams of 98% pure methamphetamine located inside a shed-like structure in the rear of the residence, where they also found other drugs including cocaine, crack cocaine, and ecstasy. Inside the shed, officers discovered a stolen Glock semi-automatic pistol. Agents found two digital scales and plastic baggies during the search. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The case was investigated by the FBI, DEA, GBI, and the Columbus Police Department. Deputy Criminal Chief Vernoica Hansis is prosecuting the case for the Government. Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Middle

title: Southern Utah Man Charged for Allegedly Receiving and Possessing Child Pornography
body: Press Release Southern Utah Man Charged for Allegedly Receiving and Possessing Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah ST. GEORGE , Utah – A Southern Utah man appeared in federal court today for his initial appearance following a federal indictment alleging he committed multiple crimes after he allegedly received and possessed child pornography, otherwise known as child sex abuse material or “CSAM.” Adam Richard Roettger Jr., 26, of St. George, Utah was indicted on October 20, 2026. According to court documents, on June 10, 2026, Roettger allegedly shared a video file which depicted a Telegram chat containing dozens of videos of child sex abuse material. On June 17, 2026, law enforcement executed a search warrant on Roettger’s residence and recovered his cellphone. On June 24, 2026, officers executed a search warrant on Roettger’s cell phone and located 16 videos and 17 photos that contained child sex abuse material. On June 26, 2026, an additional search warrant was executed on Roettger’s residence where officers recovered additional electronic devices that could contain child sex abuse material. Law enforcement performed searches on all Roettger’s devices and allegedly located approximately 316 videos and image files containing child sex abuse material. Law enforcement also allegedly located chat threads between Roettger’s devices and others discussing the trading and sharing of child sex abuse material. In at least one chat, Roettger allegedly received a file containing CSAM. U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement. Roettger is charged with receipt of child pornography and possession of child pornography. He is scheduled for a four-day jury trial beginning on January 4, 2027, at the courthouse located at 206 West Tabernacle Street, St. George, Utah 84770. The case is being investigated by the St. George Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Joseph M. Hood of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah is prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
