title: Terrorism-Linked Colombian Drug Trafficker Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Import Nearly 62 Pounds of Cocaine into U.S.
body: Press Release Terrorism-Linked Colombian Drug Trafficker Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Import Nearly 62 Pounds of Cocaine into U.S. Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California LOS ANGELES – A Colombian drug trafficker with ties to the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia – People’s Army (FARC-EP) foreign terrorist organization pleaded guilty today to federal narcotics and firearms charges, including importing 28 kilograms (61.7 pounds) of cocaine in the United States. Jorge Eliécer Luque Monsalve, 54, a.k.a. “Jorge Col,” of Santander, Colombia, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine for the purpose of unlawful importation, one count of conspiracy to possess firearms, machineguns, and destructive devices in furtherance of a drug trafficking offense, one count of distribution of cocaine for the purpose of unlawful importation, and one count of possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking offense. Luque has been in federal custody since February 5 after Colombia extradited him to the United States. According to his plea agreement, from March 2023 to March 2024, Luque conspired with drug traffickers and aided and, during the year of 2023, abetting the distribution of a total of approximately 28 kilograms (61.7 pounds) into the United States. Luque admitted to participating in a May 2023 meeting in Colombia with people he believed were buyers. During that meeting, he agreed to provide them with approximately 7 kilograms (15.4 pounds) of cocaine, knowing that it would be imported into and distributed within the United States. Luque also invested his own money into 0.5 kilogram (1.1 pounds) of the cocaine with the expectation that he would receive a share of the profits from its importation and distribution into the U.S. Three days after that meeting, Luque distributed approximately 7 kilograms of cocaine to the buyers in exchange of Colombian pesos worth approximately $10,715. In July 2023, Luque met the buyers at a mall in Colombia and accepted Colombian pesos worth approximately $4,500 as payment for his investment. In November 2023, Luque and a co-conspirator held a meeting on behalf of a leader and member of FARC-EP. The purpose of the meeting was to discuss trading cocaine for firearms. In December 2023, Luque ordered AK-47 rifles and ammunition, rocket-propelled grenade launchers and ammunition, machineguns, and additional ammunition from a buyer in exchange for 21 kilograms (46.3 pounds) of cocaine, which was distributed to a buyer. Luque in January 2024 in Colombia accepted Colombian pesos worth approximately $8,000 from buyers as payment for an investment he made in the distributed cocaine. FARC-EP is a dissident faction of the FARC terrorist group and emerged after its rejection of a 2016 peace agreement between FARC and the Colombian government. FARC-EP is Colombia’s most powerful and violent dissident group and has continued to carry out criminal acts, including assassinations, extortion, hostage-takings, and armed assaults. The group focuses most of its attacks on Colombian government and military targets but has also attacked critical infrastructure, Colombian civilians, and U.S. military personnel in the country. FARC-EP equips its members with firearms, machine guns, mines, and bombs. The group disseminates propaganda videos to convince the Colombian public and government that FARC-EP controls Colombia, to threaten rivals, and to recruit young Colombians to join it. Idrobo has appeared in and is the primary speaker in some of these videos. FARC-EP controls an area of Colombia responsible for producing approximately 70% of the cocaine manufactured in that nation. The United States has designated FARC-EP a foreign terrorist organization. FARC-EP partners with other terrorist organizations, including the Sinaloa Cartel, Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), and Nueva Familia Michoacana. United States District Judge Mark C. Scarsi scheduled a February 1, 2027, sentencing hearing at which time Luque will face a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years in federal prison and statutory maximum sentence of life imprisonment. FARC-EP commander Iván Jacobo Idrobo Arredondo, 41, a.k.a. “Marlon Vásquez,” and his associate, Juan Diego Palta Montero, 25, a.k.a. “Ñeque,” still face criminal charges in this case. Rubén Darío García Londoño, 43, a.k.a. “Bencho,” is serving a five-year federal prison sentence after pleading guilty in November 2025 to federal criminal charges in this case. The Drug Enforcement Administration’s Los Angeles Field Division and Bogotá Country Office are investigating this matter with substantial assistance from the Colombian National Police, the Czech Republic Police’s National Counterterrorism, Extremism and Cybercrime Agency (NCTEKK) and Special Activities Unit (UZC SKPV PCR). The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs and the Criminal Division’s Narcotic and Dangerous Drug Section’s Office of Judicial Attaché in Bogotá, Colombia, provided significant assistance. Assistant United States Attorneys Kyle W. Kahan of the General Crimes Section and Kelly Larocque of the Transnational Organized Crime Section are prosecuting this case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Contact Ciaran McEvoy Public Information Officer ciaran.mcevoy@usdoj.gov (213) 894-4465 Updated October 26, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Counterterrorism Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-206

title: Slidell Man Sentenced for Drug Conspiracy Involving Over 10,000 Grams of Fentanyl, a Firearm, and Money Laundering following  Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Slidell Man Sentenced for Drug Conspiracy Involving Over 10,000 Grams of Fentanyl, a Firearm, and Money Laundering following  Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS – GREGORY SMITH, JR. (“SMITH”) , age 43, of Slidell, Louisiana, was sentenced to 151 months in prison to be followed by 5 years of supervised release by United States District Judge Carl J. Barbier on October 22, 2026, after previously pleading guilty to violations of the Federal Controlled Substances Act, the Federal Gun Control Act and the Federal Money Laundering Control Act, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. SMITH previously pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute, and possess with the intent to distribute, over 400 grams of fentanyl, in violation of 21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(A), and 846. SMITH also pled guilty to one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm, in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(g)(1) and 924(a)(8). Additionally, SMITH pled guilty to three counts of engaging in monetary transactions derived from specified unlawful activity, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1957. The Court also imposed a mandatory $100 special assessment fee per count. “The shared mission of the Homeland Security Task Force is to leverage the assets of all participating partner agencies to aggressively dismantle the criminal networks that profit by pumping dangerous and potentially fatal drugs into our communities,” stated U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. “Together, we will continue to enforce the laws of the land and to protect the public that we so proudly  serve.” “Through the hard work of our Homeland Security Task Force, we dismantled not only a massive fentanyl operation, but also the elaborate financial illusion built behind it,” said Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Assistant Special Agent in Charge Randy Harness. “This defendant went to great lengths to launder drug proceeds into luxury vehicles and real estate to fund a lifestyle built on community destruction. Our federal team followed the paper trail and proved that no amount of financial maneuvering can hide illegal drug money from justice.” “Through strong law enforcement partnerships, Louisiana State Police remains committed to dismantling organized criminal networks across Louisiana, from our largest cities to our smallest towns,” said Colonel Frank Besson, Louisiana State Police Superintendent. “These investigations are only one part of the process. Working with the U.S. Attorney’s Office to successfully prosecute those responsible is essential to achieving justice and holding offenders accountable. This partnership ensures our investigative efforts carry through to the courtroom, helping protect our communities and disrupt criminal activity across the state.” According to court documents, SMITH conspired with others to distribute fentanyl in the Eastern District of Louisiana and elsewhere. On May 4, 2023, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) searched SMITH’s residence and seized approximately 10,593.572 grams of fentanyl, 3.76 grams of cocaine, marijuana, and drug paraphernalia including two digital scales with fentanyl residue, a rectangle cake pan with fentanyl residue, multiple blenders with fentanyl residue, and a vacuum sealer with fentanyl residue. Law enforcement also seized $15,520 in United States currency and a Masterpiece Arms MPA Defender, nine-millimeter semi-automatic submachine gun, with an extended magazine that contained nine-millimeter caliber cartridges. In July and August of 2021, SMITH structured cash deposits of his illegal narcotics proceeds into an account at a bank, then sent a wire to a credit union account using the funds to pay-off the balance on a car and to purchase an official check in the amount of $27,617.55 made out to a title company. The official check to the title company was used at the closing of the purchase of SMITH’s residence. SMITH also used $48,931 in illegal drug proceeds to purchase a 2018 Maserati Levante. United States Attorney David I. Courcelle praised the work of the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Louisiana State Police. Assistant United States Attorneys Rachal Cassagne and André Jones of the Narcotics Unit are in charge of the prosecution. This prosecution is a part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from the Department of Homeland Security, Federal Bureau of Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Enforcement and Removal Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, U.S. Coast Guard, Coast Guard Investigative Service and includes the Louisiana State Police, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana. *      *      * Contact Shane M. Jones Public Information Officer United States Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Louisiana United States Department of Justice Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Louisiana, Eastern
